effects: The signer sends msg.value ETH to the Disperse contract.
Each recipients[i] gets values[i] ETH from the contract.
Any ETH left in the contract after the loop goes back to the signer (msg.sender.transfer(balance)).
formats.shown: Send up to the attached ETH value in total, then one To/Amount pair per recipient in ETH.

findings.title: disperseEther: the screen does not say that leftover ETH comes back to the signer.
findings.evidence: Disperse.sol disperseEther: `if (balance > 0) msg.sender.transfer(balance);` The descriptor's sentence 'Send up to {@.value} in total' and label 'Maximum Total' only hint at a refund. Case 0 reader: 'Whether any leftover ETH is returned to me. The screen doesn't say.'
findings.fix: Optionally say it in the sentence, e.g. 'Send up to {@.value} in total; any unspent ETH is refunded'.

cases.notes: 0.215043239227074712 ETH left the signer, which matches the Maximum Total and the four amounts of 0.05376 ETH each. Nothing was refunded.

effects: The signer's allowance to Disperse for the token is spent by the sum of all values.
The signer sends the sum of all values of the token to the Disperse contract (transferFrom(msg.sender, this, total)).
Disperse sends values[i] of the token to each recipients[i].
formats.shown: Send {token} to many, then one To/Amount pair per recipient in that token. No total is shown.

findings.title: disperseToken: the total pulled from the signer is never shown because ERC-7730 cannot sum an array.
findings.evidence: Disperse.sol disperseToken: `total += values[i]; require(token.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), total));`. The descriptor only shows values.[] one by one. Case 1: the signer sent 64,205.36 USDC in one transfer, and the reader had to add up the five amounts.
findings.fix: None in the descriptor today. A sum or aggregate format in the spec would let the total go in the intent.

findings.title: disperseToken: long recipient lists turn into many field pairs that are hard to review.
findings.evidence: The descriptor's bundled iteration over recipients.[] and values.[] gives two fields per recipient. Case 1 has 10 fields for 5 recipients; batches can be much longer.
findings.fix: None in the descriptor; this depends on how wallets page arrays.

cases.notes: 64,205.36 USDC left the signer to Disperse and was split as shown. The per-recipient amounts add up exactly; the reader added them up correctly.

effects: For each i, the signer sends values[i] of the token straight to recipients[i] (transferFrom(msg.sender, recipients[i], values[i])).
The signer's allowance to Disperse for the token is spent by the sum of all values.
formats.shown: Send {token} to many, then one To/Amount pair per recipient in that token. No total is shown.

findings.title: disperseTokenSimple: no total is shown, so the signer must add up many amounts themselves.
findings.evidence: Disperse.sol disperseTokenSimple loops `token.transferFrom(msg.sender, recipients[i], values[i])`. The descriptor shows only values.[]. Case 2: 23 transfers totaling 66,688.25 AZTEC, which the reader had to add up.
findings.fix: None in the descriptor today. This waits on an aggregate or sum capability in ERC-7730.

findings.title: disperseTokenSimple: 23 recipients give 46 fields, too many to review comfortably.
findings.evidence: Case 2 screen: 46 To/Amount fields from the bundled iteration over recipients.[] and values.[].
findings.fix: None in the descriptor; this depends on how wallets page arrays.

cases.notes: All 23 AZTEC transfers from the signer match the To/Amount pairs exactly. The reader added them up to the right total of about 66,688 AZTEC.
